title: Tokyo Olympics | Medal Predictions For India’s Biggest-Ever Contingent l Can They Script History?
description: India is sending the biggest contingent at the Tokyo Olympics. With 119 players participating India will look to improve its previous best performance that came at the 2012 London Olympics. India’s medal hope will be on players like PV SIndhu, Mary Kom, Manu Bhaker and many more. But India will miss the services of Dipa Karmakar, Saina Nehwal and Sakshi Malik.  #Tokyo2020 #Olympic #India  Crux is your daily dose of the big, viral and relevant news in a few minutes. asr.full_text: Music has consistently underperformed. India is even out-performed by smaller and poorer nations like a lot of countries like Ethiopia , Kenya , and North Korea with 9 gold, 7 silver, and 12 bronze medals. India has won 28 medals since Olympics in 1900 and ranks 53rd in the overall medal tally. The Indian hockey team dominated the Olympics from 1928 to 1936, winning three titles. Their domination also continued post-independence when India beat Great Britain in the finals of the 1948 Summer Olympics to land the first gold medal for India as an independent country. India has won 8 medals in Hockey post-independence, including five gold. India's tennis sensation Leander Pace won bronze at the Atlanta Olympics in 1996. This came after India returned without a medal from three successive Olympics. Following Leander Pace's heroics, Indian athletes also won medals in wrestling, boxing and badminton in the following Olympics, with the London Olympics being the best-ever where India bagged six medals. India is expecting an improved performance in the Tokyo Olympics, especially after bagging just two medals at the Rio Olympics. And these are the disciplines where India expects podium finishes. With a 15-member squad, shooting remains India's best chance of winning a bunch of medals. The current squad is filled with young prodigies who are eager to make a name at the biggest stage of them all. A case in point is Saurabh Chaudhary. He burst onto the world stage at the 2018 Asian Games where he won gold. Since then, he has won five gold at the ISSF World Cups along with a gold medal at the Junior Olympics. Saurabh Chaudhary, Senior World Champion, ISF World Cup In 2015, I started my shooting academy in a nearby town. I started shooting in a shooting academy in my neighbouring village. My family supported me a lot. They told me that I should try when I like it so much. So I went there and tried. I started liking it and I kept doing it. And as I kept doing it off the results became better than expected have recently seen some success in world tournaments. And a closer look at the wrestlers who qualified for Tokyo Olympics reveals the secret. All the seven wrestlers hail from Haryana, where dangal happens on the mat, in the Olympic style and not on mud. This makes it easier for wrestlers from the state to adapt to the challenge. India's medal hopes will be pinned on Vinesh Pogad. A member of the illustrious Pogad family, she will look to overturn her disappointing performance in Rio where she had to bow out due to an injury. She does have a responsibility. She will have to finish what her family started. And the dream of the Olympics will end only after the medal comes. But the men's doubles pair of Satyak Sairaj, Ranki Reddy and Chirag Shetty can also not be written off. The pair won the Thailand Open Super 500, becoming the first Indian pair to win the title. The duo also broke into the top 10 in the world with a career-best ranking of 7. What makes them a promising prospect is that they didn't let COVID-19 affect their form as they reached the semi-finals in two of the four tournaments they played recently. India is sending a 228-member strong contingent for the Tokyo Olympics. This includes 119 athletes and 109 officials. Out of the 119 athletes, 67 are male and 52 are female. Here are the top five athletes who are expected to bring glory to India. The performance of Indian athletes in track and field competitions has never been up to the mark. But this medal drought could end with Neeraj Chopra. Javelin thrower Neeraj Chopra first burst into the national reckoning in 2016 when he created a new Junior World Record. His brilliance was on display in 2020 when he took part in only one tournament in 2020 and booked his place in the Olympics. Chopra also set a new national record of 88.07 at the Indian GP3 in 2021. That's our journey. We have a few years of career before we can motivate ourselves. I failed on a year in the competition due to the injuries. Then I focused for Olympics. And from another one, I did a comebacker. streak come the Olympics. She, along with Sourav Chaudhry, are favourites to win a medal for the country. They have paired together four times, and have won each time. Marry Korn returned home with the bronze in the 51-kilogram category from London 2012 Olympics. The six-time flyweight world champion will hope to replicate her performance in the Tokyo 2020 Olympics as well. This may also be the last time we see magnificent Mary at the highest level. PV Sindhu could fetch another Olympic medal in Tokyo. Sindhu recently reached the finals of the Swiss Open, followed by a semi-final entry in the All England Open Badminton Championships. But despite recent wins, her consistency has dipped. Often considered as a big match player, the country's expectations will be on her to win her second medal at the Games. I am sure, I mean, the pressure is always going to be there, you can't deny that. But it's just that, you know, when you think about that, that would add extra pressure rather, you just go on to the court with the mindset, Yeah, you just have to do well and give your best." Deepika Kumari reclaimed her world number one status after winning gold at the Archery World Cup. After a disappointing outing at Rio 2016, she will be hungry to make amends. In the 2020 Tokyo Olympics, India will be without many athletes who could have brought glory to the nation. One of the biggest heartbrake of the Rio Olympics was Deepa Karmarkar who missed a medal by point one five points but her performance was enough to push Deepa into celebrity status. However injuries plagued the gymnast from Agarthala and even though she recovered in time for the qualification tournaments the pandemic hit and all the competitions were cancelled… In place of Deepa, India's Olympic hopes now rest on the shoulders of Pranati Nayak! Sakshi Malik scripted the biggest comeback in the 2016 Olympics. Despite losing her quarter-final, Sakshi made the most of her second chance winning a bronze. However, contrary to expectations, Sakshi Malik had to settle for a bronze at the Commonwealth Games 2018 as well. Her bat form continued at the Asian Games, where Sakshi returned empty-handed. Sushil Kumar, once the most decorated Olympian, is now an accused in a murder case. The wrestler was named in an FIR in connection with the murder of 23 year old wrestler, Sagar Dhankar. It was alleged that Sushil and his associates beat up Dhankar in the parking area of a stadium leading to his death. The Olympian went missing and a lookout notice was issued following which he was arrested. The Olympics will not only be a test for the athletes, but also the Government's commitment toward developing sports in the country. The hopes of an entire nation, now rest on these 126 athletes.
